A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 51-page versions of the same AdaRoPE paper, including Appendices A–G. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable matching of equations, experiments, figures and tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic retrieval, language-model pretraining and context-extension experiments in Sections 3–5 and Tables 1–4, plus head-level analyses in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments in Sections 3–5 and Tables 1–4, together with the empirical analyses in Appendix B.

M1.justification: AdaFreq's learned head-specific frequencies, AdaScale's length-dependent temperatures, and the context-extension optimization strategies remain unchanged in Sections 3 and 5.

E1.justification: Both versions use FineWeb-Edu-100B, PG19, the same seven NLU benchmarks, WikiText-103, RULER, and the same synthetic retrieval and needle-retrieval scenarios, including Appendix B.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains RoPE, PRoPE, ALiBi and NoPE. Tables 2–4 retain the same backbone, YaRN and LoRA training-strategy comparisons; comparator membership in the appendix analyses also matches.

E3.justification: The metrics, model configurations, 100B-token pretraining, 5-shot NLU/0-shot Lambada evaluation, 8k-to-64k extension, 100-sample adaptation and 600M-token continued-pretraining protocols are unchanged, as are Appendix G settings.

E4.justification: The component and training-strategy ablations in Tables 1–4 are retained. Appendix B contains the same window-size, frequency-specialization, effective-length and per-head influence analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version adds or revises repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval or significance-testing information. Existing reporting practices, including Figure 3's summaries and quantile bands across heads, are identical.

E6.justification: The empirical values and findings in Tables 1–4 and Figures 1–12 match. For example, Table 2 reports the same LLaMA 8B RULER-64k scores: 51.87 for AdaRoPE and 12.80 for Backbone+YaRN.

T1.justification: Theorems 4–5 in Appendix E.4 and their restatements change convergence from 'as d, L → ∞' to 'as d → ∞ then L → ∞'. Appendix F.6 replaces the Slutsky step with continuous-mapping and Portmanteau arguments; F.7 invokes that revised reasoning. This is a localized correction to the limiting regime and proof, with the scaling formulas and remaining theory retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about head heterogeneity, learnable per-head adaptation, improved pretraining and effective context extension.

C2.justification: Interpretations of frequency specialization, attention dilution, positional warm-up and short-/long-context trade-offs remain unchanged in Sections 4–5 and Appendix B. The formal limit correction introduces no accompanying revision to the interpretive discussion.

D1.justification: Section 3.4's implementation and overhead details and Appendix G's tokenizer, model configurations, optimizers, learning rates, schedules and LoRA settings are identical. Code and data access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: Related-work positioning and cited-work membership are unchanged. The Su et al. (2021) RoFormer entry revises author and bibliographic metadata while retaining the same work and arXiv identifier.

P1.justification: Local edits expand the proof exposition in Appendices F.6–F.7, revise the RoFormer bibliography entry and update the arXiv version/date stamp. The main narrative, section order and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Expanded proof displays reflow text and equations across pages 46–50, and the shortened RoFormer entry slightly changes reference spacing on page 12. All figures and tables retain their design and placement.

improvement.justification: v2 improves theoretical precision by specifying sequential dimension-then-length limits in Theorems 4–5 and supplying the continuous-mapping/Portmanteau justification missing from v1's Slutsky step. The guarantee is narrower but better aligned with the argument. This provides a limited improvement in rigor while the method and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
